Marissa / Rishi - quick tech answers below; attaching a short PDF with sample Node snippets and rotation patterns. See attached 'redwood_api_key_rotation.pdf'.

1) Service accounts & short-lived tokens:
   - Redwood supports JWT-based service accounts. Customers can mint short-lived JWTs via our token exchange endpoint (/v1/token-exchange) that are valid up to configurable TTL (we recommend 1h for prod).
   - Option A (recommended): Redwood-managed service account + short-lived tokens; integrates with AWS KMS for envelope encryption.
   - Option B: BYO KMS + HSM: customer rotates keys in their KMS and Redwood pulls verification metadata via provided public jwks endpoint.

2) API keys vs tokens:
   - API keys are persistent and OK for dev/staging. For production use, we recommend short-lived tokens to reduce blast radius. Keys can be rotated programmatically via the Admin API.

3) Rotation patterns / tooling:
   - We provide built-in rotation scheduler for Redwood-managed keys and a sample script to rotate keys every 90 days. For BYO KMS, we provide a verification handshake and webhook to notify about key rollover.

4) Client-side config (Node sample notes):
   - Use the Redwood Node SDK's auth adapter: set AUTH_STRATEGY = 'service_account_jwt' and tokenRefreshHandler to call /v1/token-exchange whenever the token is near expiry.
   - Example config snippet included in attached PDF (also shows how to set preferred model routing policy: prefer-cost then latency fallback).

5) Entitlements / differences:
   - Hosted API: supports short-lived tokens and API keys out-of-the-box. BYO KMS for verification requires Enterprise/Private entitlements.
   - Dedicated: supports same features, plus local KMS integration when deployed in-customer VPC, and SLA guarantees for token exchange throughput.

Links:
- Integration guide: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/redwood-integration-specs
- Token exchange spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth/token-exchange
